questions.question: What type of memory allows comparison of desired bit locations within a word for a specified match across all words simultaneously?
questions.explanation:
Associative access is a random access memory that enables simultaneous comparison of bit locations within all words. (Source Page: [114])  

---

questions.question: In cache organization, if the cache line field is r bits, how many distinct cache lines can be identified?
questions.explanation:
The line field of r bits identifies one of m = 2ʳ lines of the cache. (Source Page: [126])  

---

questions.question: Which term describes the permission to delete data from a memory location?
The smallest location that can be uniquely addressed in external memory is called the:
questions.explanation:
The addressable unit is defined as the smallest location which can be uniquely addressed. (Source Page: [113])  

---

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor considered when designing a memory hierarchy?
questions.explanation:
Capacity, cost, and speed are vital roles in memory hierarchy design; chip color is irrelevant. (Source Page: [113])  

---

questions.question: In the cache logic described, the tag consists of which portion of the address bits?
questions.explanation:
The cache logic interprets the s bits as a tag of (s‑r) most significant bits. (Source Page: [126])  

---

questions.question: Which of the following best describes “interleaved” organization of memory?

options.A: Bits are stored in a single contiguous block.
options.B: Bits are physically arranged into words in a non‑obvious pattern.
options.C: Each word is stored on a separate chip.

questions.explanation:
Interleaved organization refers to a physical arrangement of bits into words that is not always obvious. (Source Page: [115])  

---

questions.question: When data is transferred from external memory to the CPU, it is typically moved in units larger than a single word. This unit is called a:
questions.explanation:
External memory transfers data in blocks larger than a word. (Source Page: [113])  

---

questions.question: Power consumption in a memory system refers to:

options.A: The speed at which data is accessed.
options.B: The amount of electricity the memory uses.
options.C: The number of bits stored per word.
options.D: The hierarchical level of the memory.

questions.explanation: Power consumption is defined as how much power the memory consumes. (Source Page: [115])
